title: Coefficient-resolution square for exact pro-etale tensor pullback
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes with small pro-etale sites, $R_Y$ a sheaf of commutative rings and $c:f^{-1}R_Y\simeq R_X$ an identification. Let $F=f_R^*$ be exact identified-coefficient module inverse image and $L:D(R_Y)\to D(R_X)$ its ordinary uncompleted unbounded derived functor [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Write $Q_Z$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms in the module categories and $\epsilon_C:LQ_YC\simeq Q_XFC$ for the exact termwise localization factors. Use sheafified tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], direct-sum total tensor of complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and the canonical two-flat-term-K-flat-representative tensor isomorphisms and derived pullback tensor comparison $\tau$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].

Let $P$ be a flat-term K-flat complex of $R_Y$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], $N$ an arbitrary $R_Y$-module sheaf, and $q:H\to N[0]$ any quasi-isomorphism with $H$ flat-term K-flat [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. Let $\sigma_{C,D}:F\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes D)\simeq\operatorname{Tot}(FC\otimes FD)$ be the ordinary total tensor comparison induced by inverse image of sheaf tensors. Its sheaf components send inverse-image unit tensors to tensors of inverse-image units. Then the following is a commuting square of complexes:
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
F\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes H)&\xrightarrow{\sigma_{P,H}}&\operatorname{Tot}(FP\otimes FH)\\
\downarrow F(1_P\otimes q)&&\downarrow 1_{FP}\otimes Fq\\
F(P\otimes N)&\xrightarrow{\sigma_{P,N[0]}}&FP\otimes FN.
\end{array}$$
Both vertical arrows are quasi-isomorphisms. The total tensors in the top row, and their inverse images as applicable, are flat-term K-flat. Under the canonical two-representative tensor isomorphisms and $\epsilon$, the localized top arrow is exactly $\tau_{Q_YP,Q_YH}$.

Define $\alpha_Y:Q_Y(P\otimes N)\simeq Q_YP\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_Y}Q_Y(N[0])$ to be the composite $Q_Y(1_P\otimes q)^{-1}$, the canonical two-representative isomorphism for $(P,H)$, and $1\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q_Yq$. Define $\alpha_X$ by the same formula for $(FP,FH,Fq)$, identifying $F(N[0])$ with $(FN)[0]$. These maps are independent of $q$, and the following equality holds in $D(R_X)$:
$$\alpha_X\circ Q_X(\sigma_{P,N[0]})\circ\epsilon_{P\otimes N}
=(\epsilon_P\otimes^{\mathbf L}\epsilon_{N[0]})\circ\tau_{Q_YP,Q_Y(N[0])}\circ L(\alpha_Y).$$
No boundedness or flatness of $N$ is assumed, and $P\otimes N$ need not be K-flat over $R_Y$.

proof.text: The fixed-K-flat tensor theorem preserves every quasi-isomorphism in the other factor. Applied to P and q it gives u=1 tensor q quasi-isomorphic. Exact termwise pullback preserves u and q. Apply the same fixed-tensor theorem to FP and Fq to obtain v=1 tensor Fq quasi-isomorphic. Hence Q(u) and Q(v) have the specified asIso inverses eY and eX.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product, representative construction and its naturality

proof.text: For a fixed flat-term K-flat complex P, let T(M)=Tot(P tensor M). Since T preserves quasi-isomorphisms, use localization to obtain a functor Hb on the derived category with phi:Q Hb isomorphic to T Q. On flat-term K-flat H, the given representative comparison yields a natural isomorphism phi followed by r(P,H) from Q Hb to the prescribed tensor(QP,QH). Extend it by fully faithful restriction on pairs, using the second projection and fixing the first object QP. Full faithfulness follows from the resolving-representative theorem: every homotopy object has a flat-term K-flat resolution. Whiskering the resulting isomorphism with Q and composing with phi inverse gives d:T Q isomorphic to Q tensor(QP,-), with d_H=r(P,H). Naturality at any resolution q:H to M implies alpha=e.inv r(P,H) tensor(1,Qq)=d_M. Thus alpha is independent of the resolution and every allowed inverse witness, over both sites. Its invertibility also follows directly from the invertibility of its three factors.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product, representative construction and its naturality

proof.text: Precompose the final asserted identity by the invertible L(Q(u)). Naturality of epsilon at u and the localized chain square turn its left side into epsilon_T Q(sigma_PH) r_X tensor(1,QFq), cancelling Q(v) with eX inverse. Substitute the top representative square. Naturality of epsilon at q and bifunctoriality combine tensor(epsilon_P,epsilon_H) with tensor(1,QFq) into tensor(1,LQq) followed by tensor(epsilon_P,epsilon_M). Naturality of tau moves the first factor across tau. Finally functoriality of L and cancellation of Q(u) with eY inverse give the right side. No step requires flatness of N or K-flatness of Tot(P tensor N[0]).
